title: The locus of the base where a closed map becomes unramified is an open subspace with the universal property

standard_prerequisites.use: Morphisms of Spaces, lemma where-unramified (the unramified-locus open and its base-change compatibility); Properties of Spaces, lemmas open-subspaces and factor-through-open-subspace (the dictionary between open subspaces and their point sets, and the factoring criterion).

core_obligations: Import the functorial unramified locus of the map.
Push the complement of that locus down along the closed map to carve W out of Z.
Verify the universal factoring property through base-change stability.

proof_roadmap.step: Closed-image complement descending the universal property to W.

difficulty_reason: For a commutative diagram of algebraic spaces X -> Y -> Z with p : X -> Z locally of finite type and closed, the lemma produces an open subspace W of Z such that a morphism Z' -> Z factors through W exactly when the base changed map X_{Z'} -> Y_{Z'} is unramified. The retained proof is written: the where-unramified open U(f) of X exists with base-change-stable formation (Morphisms of Spaces, lemma where-unramified); define W as the open subspace (Properties of Spaces, lemma open-subspaces) whose points are Z minus the closed image p(|X| \ |U(f)|) — closedness of p is what makes the complement open; the universal property follows from the base-change stability of U(f) plus the factor-through-open-subspace criterion (Properties of Spaces, lemma factor-through-open-subspace). Retained author proof at lines 11543-11563.

dedup.scope: Universal open of the base parametrizing unramifiedness after base change for closed maps of spaces.
